title: UCLA students protest in solidarity with Palestinians on October 7 anniversary
seoTitle: Los Angeles: UCLA students protest Palestine

summary: On October 7, 2026, students at the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) organized a pro-Palestinian protest. The demonstration, hosted by Students for Justice in Palestine at UCLA, marked the third anniversary of the October 7 attacks. Organizers stated their purpose was to commemorate "three years of escalated genocide in Palestine" and to honor "martyrs," aiming to recognize and uplift Palestinian resistance and work towards "liberation," according to Daily Mail. Approximately 75 students and supporters gathered on campus, chanting slogans such as "Long live the intifada!" and "From the river to the sea, Palestine will be free," as reported by the New York Post. About 25 UCLA police officers and public safety aides monitored the event.
organizers: Students for Justice in Palestine at UCLA
demands: Recognition and upliftment of Palestinian resistance
End to university investment in "war and weapons"
response: UCLA police officers and public safety aides monitored the demonstration, with Richard Mejia, director of emergency communications for UCLA, stating it was "one of many First Amendment demonstrations that happen on campus year-round." (Source 2)

crowd.text: A group of about 75 students and other supporters gathered on the university grounds (Source 2)

updates.text: Students for Justice in Palestine at UCLA organized a protest on campus, scheduled for 12pm PDT, to commemorate the October 7 anniversary. (Source 1)
About 75 students and supporters protested at UCLA, monitored by approximately 25 police officers and public safety aides. (Source 2)
Protesters chanted slogans including "Long live the intifada!" and "From the river to the sea, Palestine will be free." (Source 2)
An Israeli student group, Bruins for Israel, planned a vigil for later in the evening to remember those lost on October 7th. (Source 1)
